topic: DeepSeek V4 Pro NVFP4: which GPUs can load it
title: DeepSeek V4 Pro NVFP4: Which GPUs Fit?
description: The 4-bit cut of DeepSeek V4 Pro still weighs 941 GB, because mixture-of-experts models keep every expert in memory. The format shrinks the file, not the hardware tier: only a 512 GB Mac Studio clears the weights alone.
hook_text: Your GPU was never the problem.
hook_candidates: Your GPU was never the problem. *
The 4-bit cut that still needs a datacenter.
NVFP4, explained in one file size.
Read this before the 941 GB download.
Quantization shrinks the file, not the tier.
One terabyte, four bits, zero gaming cards.
Stop guessing if it fits. Do the math.
narration_full: You checked if DeepSeek's biggest model fits your card. It is nine hundred forty-one gigabytes on disk. The consensus: four-bit, so it fits. Quantization stores weights in fewer bits; the file shrinks, not the count. Picture a company of specialists; a receptionist wakes the few each word needs. She re-picks every time. Forty-nine billion parameters answer one word; the whole staff fills memory. NVIDIA's biggest workstation card: ninety-six gigabytes of memory. A desktop box reaches one hundred twenty-eight gigabytes of memory. Only a Mac Studio with five hundred twelve gigabytes of memory clears the weights alone, before the chat's memory joins. So match your memory tier first, because four-bit never promised fit.

notes_for_review: Unverified items kept out: no throughput claims, no llama.cpp/Ollama/LM Studio loading claims, no SM120 rejection reports, no 2 TB disk figure. Only the five assigned numbers are spoken; 1.65T and benchmark deltas appear nowhere. RTX PRO 6000, DGX Spark and NVFP4 are named on screen only. The trade-off lands as conversation-memory headroom after the weights; the analogy's limit (re-picking per word) is stated in s03.
